items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The context is the mortal world among lowest men
items.inference: This teaching should be carefully hidden from unworthy people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching be given after proper testing?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Only a previously accomplished person tested for one year is fit to receive it.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is described as emerged from Candradvīpa
The section is identified as fifth
The section is called a chapter
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the fifth chapter of the Candradvīpa text.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: What understanding has been gained through the grace of the lord of Kaulas?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
The object known is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: By the lord's grace, the speaker has understood the Kaula doctrine.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the identity and essential nature of the soul as declared?
premises: The soul has been declared in teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The verse asks for clarification of both who the soul is and what its nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul's dissolution is questioned
The locus of dissolution is asked for
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The speaker seeks a full account of where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that soul?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme
The soul is described as partless and eternal
The soul is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The soul's essential nature is transcendent, undivided, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from affliction, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in relation to haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is called supreme
That same soul is identified as haṃsa
It is also described as power and individual
items.inference: The supreme soul is equated with haṃsa as the individual locus of power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated in living beings?
premises: The vital air is described as filled with breath
It is present in all beings
It is said to be situated there
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides within all living beings.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body
The subject is then designated anew
The designation is supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon leaving the body, that soul is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and perceived according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes through successive tradition
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: This knowledge is received aurally through an unbroken traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the immediate effect of merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The cause is this knowledge alone
The knowledge is received by hearing
The addressee is directly addressed
items.inference: Even mere hearing of this knowledge has a significant effect.
uncertainties: The specific effect is completed in the following verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard,

items.question: What practice over six months leads to freedom from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner is described as one who practices
The state attained is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The role of kāṣāyaṃ is ambiguous and may be metaphorical or literal.
items.plain_english: one who practices for six months becomes free from bondage.

items.question: What benefits result from this practice regarding health and yogic companionship?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
Union with yogis is presented as an outcome
items.inference: The practice yields freedom from disease and communion with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī
The subject communicated is the practice of the soul
The communication is declared complete
items.inference: The instruction on the practice concerning the soul has been conveyed to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved practitioner may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to a fully prepared and resolute practitioner.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a firm resolve.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
Its origin is from the yoginīs
It is explicitly declared not to be given
items.inference: The sacred Kaula essence of yoginī origin must not be disclosed to the unfit.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is struck away?
premises: The speaker refers to her own body
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The body is now declared pure
items.inference: The removal of ignorance has rendered the speaker's body pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time is now sought?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish to hear
The topic concerns time
The desired knowledge is the auspicious deception of time
items.inference: The speaker now seeks instruction on how to overcome or outwit time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the possibility of destroying death?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
The explanation concerns how death is destroyed
items.inference: The teaching will certainly explain the means by which death is overcome.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: What paradoxical condition affects even the wise at the source of nectar?
premises: The context is the tip or source of nectar
There is contact with the essence of juice
Even a wise person is described as burning
items.inference: Even the wise may experience a burning condition at the nectar's source.
uncertainties: The physiological or yogic referent of amṛta+agraṃ is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one, at the tip of nectar, is burned by the essence of that juice.

items.question: What yogic technique involving breath at the palate is prescribed to counter this condition?
premises: The locus is the root of tongue and palate
The practitioner acts upon the breath
The breath should be drawn in slowly
items.inference: One should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing the breath at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink it in.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are said to be destroyed
items.inference: A year of this practice leads to the destruction of old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for one established in this practice?
premises: The threat is poison from great serpents
Even being bitten is conceded
Poison does not enter the body
items.inference: The accomplished practitioner remains unaffected by venom even when bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
